nodes.label: Repair unwraps JSON-Schema-shaped {type,value} args
nodes.rationale: The PR-7 spike observed small models emitting {"type":"integer","value":15} for a plain dc, for strings as well as numbers. Unwrapping it in the repair layer keeps a valid tool call instead of a rejected one.

nodes.label: Numeric string coerced to number, non-numeric string is not
nodes.rationale: Repair must be narrow: '25' -> 25 is safe, 'a lot' -> NaN would silently corrupt the ledger, so it stays unrepairable.

nodes.label: Hallucinated extra keys are dropped, call stays valid
nodes.rationale: Models add fields like `confidence`; rejecting the whole call for them would cost a turn.

nodes.label: Unrepairable args return ok:false, never throw
nodes.rationale: A throw kills the turn; an {ok:false,error} lets the caller hand the model an `ERROR: ...` tool result so it self-corrects. Covers missing required fields, bad enum values, and non-object arguments (bare string, array, null).

nodes.label: Assistant text segments get a blank-line separator, never bare glue
nodes.rationale: Playtest screenshot regression: two text segments of one assistant message concatenated mid-sentence ('do?The priest draws a breath'). Appends directly only when `existing` already ends in whitespace.

nodes.label: Referee content never reaches onDelta; only narrator prose does
nodes.rationale: The two-phase contract: referee runs the agentic tool loop and its beat sheet is internal; narrator is a second, tools-free completion whose stream is what the player reads. onToolUse still fires for referee tool calls so the dice UI works.

nodes.label: Narrator request carries no tools/tool_choice and uses narratorModel
nodes.rationale: Keeps mechanics strictly on the referee model; the narrator cannot mutate state even if it tries.

nodes.label: Referee is nudged exactly once when a turn resolved no tools
nodes.rationale: Live 'I drink a tincture to heal' turn: the referee wrote a beat sheet and called nothing, so HP/inventory never moved while the narrator described the heal as having happened. One nudge, then it accepts a genuinely mechanics-free turn -- and the narrator is told 'resolved NOTHING mechanical this turn' so it cannot invent one.

nodes.label: Missing defeat_foe / apply_damage nudge keys off mechanics, not prose
nodes.rationale: Live failure: the referee rolled the kill, wrote 'dead before he hits the ground', called nothing -- 0 XP and no foe record. Prompting did not fix it, so the code checks what the prompt cannot. The first attempt keyed off beat-sheet wording and missed 'collapses lifelessly'; it now fires on a landed attack regardless of phrasing, stays quiet on a miss or when damage already landed, does not read the hero going down as a victory, and nudges at most once per turn.

nodes.label: roller:'player' pauses the dual turn before the narrator phase
nodes.rationale: Neither the referee's follow-up step nor the narrator may run until the player's roll resolves, or the prose would describe an outcome the player has not rolled yet.

nodes.label: Referee-phase and narrator-phase HTTP failures both surface as DmError
nodes.rationale: A 401 in the referee phase must classify as 'auth' and never reach the narrator; a narrator-phase 503 must still end the turn with busy cleared rather than hanging.

nodes.label: interrupt() aborts in flight without onError/onTurnComplete
nodes.rationale: A deliberate abort is not a failure: it must clear busy, fire no callbacks, and must not be reported as a provider stall.

nodes.label: Narrator falls back to openai.model with a friendly system note
nodes.rationale: An unset narratorModel degrades to the referee's model rather than erroring, and says so once at start().

nodes.label: Empty narration retried within a budget, then given up honestly
nodes.rationale: Free-tier providers intermittently return a stream with no content, which killed the turn outright. Initial + NARRATOR_EMPTY_RETRIES attempts, then a 'returned nothing' error rather than a loop.

nodes.label: A stream that opens and goes silent is broken by a stall timeout
nodes.rationale: Live: a provider opened a stream and never sent a byte, leaving the game 'thinking' for five minutes with only STOP as a way out. The error names which phase (referee) went quiet and clears busy.

nodes.label: Narrator prompt carries the hero's real post-turn numbers
nodes.rationale: Regression: the narrator wrote 'your HP climbs to eleven of thirteen' and described a tincture being drained on a turn where no tool ran, so the prose and the character sheet disagreed and the prose won in the player's head. The prompt now embeds HP x/y, the Carrying list, a GROUND TRUTH block, and an explicit 'has NOT taken effect' warning when no tools ran; it also strips the referee-only <system-reminder> out of the player text and forbids suggesting uncarried items.

nodes.label: describeCondition states CONSCIOUS/DOWN outright, never inferable
nodes.rationale: Live defect: handed a bare 'HP 5/12' the narrator wrote a death scene on a turn where the attack MISSED. Any hp>0 reads CONSCIOUS and forbids collapse; only hp<=0 reads DOWN and permits death; wording scales unhurt/lightly hurt/wounded/badly wounded; maxHp 0 must not divide by zero.

nodes.label: Tool outcomes render one line each, failures marked distinctly
nodes.rationale: The narrator needs to see a FAILED call as a failure, not as something that happened; an empty turn reads '(no tool calls this turn)'.

nodes.label: Content deltas stream through and the turn completes without tools
A tool call runs the same handler the Claude backend uses
nodes.rationale: One handler for both backends is what keeps engine mutations identical across them. The follow-up request must also carry the assistant tool_calls message and the tool result under the same tool_call_id, in that order.

nodes.label: roller:'player' parks the agentic loop until the hook resolves
nodes.rationale: The second request must not be sent while the player still owes a roll.

nodes.label: A 401 classifies as an auth DmError and clears busy
interrupt() aborts without retrying and without callbacks
nodes.rationale: An abort is not a failure to retry -- exactly one fetch may have happened.

nodes.label: One retry on 5xx/network, none on 4xx or abort
nodes.rationale: Shared PR-8 fault-tolerance policy used by both the streaming DM loop and the summarizer's one-shot call; the budget is bounded so a failing endpoint cannot loop.

nodes.label: Transient upstream 429 retried; daily-quota/billing 429 is terminal
nodes.rationale: Free-tier reality: a shared upstream pool throttles for a few seconds, and an unretried 429 there cost a whole turn mid-scene in a live playtest. A daily-quota 429 is the opposite -- retrying only delays an error the player needs to see, so its body must stay readable.

nodes.label: Retry-After parsed from seconds or HTTP-date, clamped
nodes.rationale: An absurd advertised wait (600s) clamps to 8s so a turn never hangs on the provider's say-so; nonsense and negative values return undefined, a past date returns 0.

nodes.label: SSE decoder buffers partial lines and survives malformed data
nodes.rationale: Wire chunks split mid-JSON; keep-alive and unparseable lines must be skipped without throwing, and [DONE] is emitted as a sentinel rather than JSON.parse'd.

nodes.label: Parallel tool_calls reassembled per index from arbitrary chunking
nodes.rationale: Real streams split id/name/arguments of two parallel calls across interleaved chunks. Index order (0 before 1) must be preserved regardless of arrival order, and the assembled arguments must be parseable JSON.

nodes.label: Narration-length rule is a default that yields, not a ceiling
nodes.rationale: The old hard ceiling flatly contradicted the R clause's 'write explicit scenes in full, no cutaway' -- and the ceiling won: every intimate turn came back at ~90 words and stopped to ask 'What do you do?'. A more permissive model would not have fixed that. PG-13's own ceiling stays untouched.

nodes.label: Precomputed ability modifiers ride in the opening prompt and every turn
nodes.rationale: A fresh DM never has to ask for stats, and withMechanicsReminder re-sends mods/HP/AC/luck each turn because small models obey the last message.

nodes.label: Context brief keeps a bounded verbatim window, never zero entries
nodes.rationale: Default cap of 10 individual lines, an explicit maxVerbatimExchanges override, and at least the single most recent entry even when it alone blows the char budget.

nodes.label: Context brief forbids restating/recapping what the player already read
nodes.rationale: The old closing line plus a blank story log gave the DM every incentive to re-narrate the scene the player had already read; it now also forbids repeating the same beat twice in one reply while keeping the 'What do you do?' hook.

nodes.label: Trailer is asked for in the exact format the parser accepts, and only of player-facing prompts
nodes.rationale: The suggested-actions trailer is the one sanctioned exception to the no-choice-menus rule, so both halves must hold at once: ask for it AND keep forbidding enumerated options in the prose. The documented example must round-trip through splitSuggestions, the trailer must come last so streaming can cut it, and the referee (who writes nothing the player reads) is never asked for one.

nodes.label: Playtest-driven mechanics guardrails in every tool-owning prompt
nodes.rationale: Each assertion mirrors a defect seen in a live 10-turn playtest on free models: damage applied the same turn it is rolled, XP/quests actually recorded, no rolls for trivial actions, enemy rolls kept off the player's dice tray, no invented rewards, and a FAILED check reading as a failure. A refactor that quietly drops one should fail.

nodes.label: Prompt names award_gold/spend_gold and bans modify_gold
nodes.rationale: Second live playtest: the referee read 'I pocket the ten gold pieces' as modify_gold(-10), leaving the hero poorer for looting. Direction now comes from which tool is named, and picking things up is explicitly not a check.

nodes.label: Prompt states what an ordinary foe defends at (11-13)
nodes.rationale: Five straight live misses at DC 16 for a level-1 melee swing: the DC scale existed but said nothing about routine enemies, so the referee pitched a roadside bandit like plate armour. It now says 'the DC was wrong, not the dice'.

nodes.label: Trailer parsing tolerates sloppy small-model formatting
nodes.rationale: Case, spacing, a missing colon, quoted/bulleted/numbered items and a trailing pipe all still parse; caps at three, clamps an over-long one to 40 chars with an ellipsis, and strips a misplaced mid-prose trailer rather than leaving the marker visible.

nodes.label: Every prefix of the marker is withheld from the live stream
nodes.rationale: Deltas arrive a few characters at a time, so suppressing only the whole marker would let '[[SUG' flash on screen. visibleStreamText also never grows the text it was given, and ordinary bracketed prose passes through.

nodes.label: Chronicler prompt keeps its exact framing and skips system entries
nodes.rationale: Faithfulness instruction, oldest-first PLAYER:/DM: lines, the '(none yet)' placeholder for an empty rollup, and the exact CHAPTER SUMMARY:/STORY SO FAR: markers the parser keys on.

nodes.label: Summarizer reply parsing degrades gracefully on marker drift
nodes.rationale: Small models drop or re-case the markers. Missing STORY SO FAR falls back to the prior rollup (or the chapter text when that is empty); no markers at all makes the whole reply the chapter; neither field may ever come back empty for non-empty input.

nodes.label: dmBackend:'dual' summarizes over HTTP, never the Claude SDK
nodes.rationale: The routing had no coverage and a real bug hid in the gap: summarizeChunk branched on dmBackend === 'openai' only, so 'dual' -- the configuration actually in use -- fell through to the Claude Agent SDK. Locally that billed Claude tokens on a backend picked to bill none; on the headless cloud host with no Claude Code login it threw on every chronicle update, so lastSummarizedIndex never advanced and resume replayed the whole transcript.

nodes.label: The referee model summarizes, not the narrator model
nodes.rationale: Faithful structured summarization is the reliable tool-caller's job; the permissive narrator model is chosen for prose, not accuracy. An explicit model override still wins on both OpenAI paths.

nodes.label: dmBackend:'claude' still routes to the Agent SDK with no HTTP call
nodes.rationale: The dual fix must not have moved the Claude path; an endpoint HTTP failure surfaces as a throw the controller can catch.

nodes.label: 13 OpenAI schemas match createDmTools().tools exactly
nodes.rationale: Schemas are derived FROM the same zod shapes the Claude backend's MCP server uses, so the two backends can never silently drift apart (PR-6). Same names, same order, well-formed function entries with no $schema leak, and required fields matching exactly the non-optional zod fields.

nodes.label: interactiveRoll is used only for roller:'player'
nodes.rationale: roller:'dm' and an omitted roller both fall through to the engine even when a hook is registered, so enemy rolls never land on the player's dice tray. An ok:false from the hook surfaces as an isError CallToolResult carrying ERROR text.

nodes.label: roll_dice schema demands a 3-6 word reason, never a sentence
nodes.rationale: Bug fix: a sentence-length reason pushed the roll result off screen.

nodes.label: onLedger fires exactly once per successful gain/loss, never on failure
nodes.rationale: The web front-end renders a 'YOU GAINED' toast from the structured LedgerDelta instead of parsing engine message strings. Rejected amounts, unaffordable spends and failed removals must emit nothing, and absent hooks must never throw.

nodes.label: Gold direction comes from the tool, not the sign of the amount
nodes.rationale: The bug this pair of tools exists to make impossible: a live referee answered 'I pocket the ten gold pieces' with modify_gold(-10), so looting a corpse left the hero poorer. award_gold(-10) must still make them richer.

nodes.label: defeat_foe pays XP and records the foe in one call
nodes.rationale: Ten live turns killed a bandit on a natural 20, confirmed and looted the body, and XP never left 0 because award_xp is bookkeeping a small model drops. Non-lethal outcomes map to the right NPC status ('fled' -> missing, 'surrendered' -> alive) and a level-up still reports through the ledger.

nodes.label: defeat_foe matches a loosely-named foe already on the roster
nodes.rationale: A live kill of the world's 'Trail bandit' came back as 'Bandit', leaving two records -- one dead, one still walking around. When the reference is ambiguous (two bandits) it creates a separate record rather than killing the wrong NPC.

nodes.label: upsert_quest round-trips reward and never clears it on update
shouldSummarize counts only unsummarized non-system entries
nodes.rationale: Both thresholds are inclusive at the boundary, system entries are excluded from char sum and count alike, and only entries strictly after lastSummarizedIndex are considered.

nodes.label: Session rotation waits for the in-flight turn before end()
nodes.rationale: The player keeps playing against the old session while the summarizer call is in flight; the chronicle may mutate but the old session must not end mid-turn.

nodes.label: Post-rotation actions get the brief prepended, players see only their own text
nodes.rationale: The new memory-less session needs [CAMPAIGN BRIEFING ...] plus the wire-only mechanics reminder, but the story log and transcript must record only the player's own words -- never the brief.

nodes.label: A failed summarize leaves lastSummarizedIndex alone and retries later
nodes.rationale: No chapter, no rotation, a '(chronicle update failed -- will retry later)' note, and a naturally-retried attempt on the next completed turn since the threshold is still crossed.

nodes.label: An action submitted mid-swap is queued and flushed to the new session
nodes.rationale: There is a narrow window where the old session has ended and the new one is not up; a submission there must not be dropped.

nodes.label: shutdown() awaits an in-flight rotation instead of racing it
nodes.rationale: A /quit during a stuck summarizer must not touch session 0; rotation runs to completion and shutdown then ends the rotated-TO session, not session 0 twice.

nodes.label: Construction and pre-start() calls are inert
nodes.rationale: No AI session, engine or timers on construct; blank input, pre-start() input and busy input are all no-ops; interrupt()/shutdown() before start() resolve silently; forceSave() works before start().

nodes.label: confirmRoll/resolvePendingRoll orchestrate the luck reroll
nodes.rationale: No dc means no verdict and immediate resolution; a failed dc with luck>0 offers a reroll without resolving yet; luck 0 resolves immediately; resolvePendingRoll(false) spends nothing; resolvePendingRoll(true) spends exactly 1 luck and keeps the better of the two totals, reporting both structurally.

nodes.label: Interrupt or DM error abandons a pending roll without resolving it
nodes.rationale: The roll prompt is cleared and input re-enabled; the pending promise is abandoned, never completed with a fabricated result.

nodes.label: A failed turn is persisted to the story and to the server log
nodes.rationale: A new campaign whose opening turn failed left NOTHING anywhere: the transient note vanished on reload and nothing reached the process log -- one sat blank for 40 minutes until its owner typed something and got a reply 7 seconds later, with no record to diagnose from. The note is now worded for where it happened (opening scene vs 'did not go through') and a [dm-error] line carries kind + raw message.

nodes.label: Resume does not re-send an action a recorded failure already answered
nodes.rationale: The quota burn: a failed turn left the player's line last, resume read that as 'the DM never replied' and re-sent it, so every reopen spent another turn of a 50/day free quota on a turn that had already failed. A genuine quit-right-after-acting must still be picked up.

nodes.label: Resume shows the last scene and waits; only a dangling player line is sent
nodes.rationale: Resuming used to immediately bill a fresh, unwanted 'what happens next' turn on top of the just-replayed scene. A DM-terminated tail sends nothing and leaves busy false; the held brief is prepended to the player's next action instead. State is still pushed to the UI on load so the character panel is not empty on open.

nodes.label: Resume replays only the un-summarized transcript tail, with fresh ids
nodes.rationale: Resume used to start with a BLANK story log and hand the memory-less session its own last narration plus 'resume... end with What do you do?', inviting it to re-narrate (and, per dm.ts's appendTurnText fix, sometimes glue) the scene the player already read. Replayed ids never collide with a later live append; 'new-hero' replays too, 'new' never does.

nodes.label: A dice result is a story entry at the point it was rolled
nodes.rationale: The web client used to get rolls only as a strip pinned under the input showing the LATEST one, so a roll sat there for turns after its scene ended, attached to nothing. It is now appended and persisted in transcript order.

nodes.label: Roll entries are kept out of the DM context brief
nodes.rationale: The DM already saw every roll as a tool result; replaying them in the brief would double-count them.

nodes.label: The SUGGEST trailer never reaches story, transcript or screen
nodes.rationale: The marker is machine-read only: leaking it makes it prose in the story the player reads and in the history the DM is later fed back (context brief and chronicle summarizer). Chips are also cleared when the player acts so a previous scene's options cannot linger.

nodes.label: defaultSessionFactory maps dmBackend to the right session class
nodes.rationale: 'claude' -> DmSession, 'openai' -> OpenAiDmSession, 'dual' -> DualModelDmSession. loadSettings is mocked so the test never reads a real settings.json or env.

nodes.label: Dice expression parsing enforces count/sides/modifier bounds
nodes.rationale: Whitespace and case tolerated; d1, 0d6, 101d6, a 2000 modifier, a dangling '+' and negative dice all rejected as null rather than parsed loosely.

nodes.label: Advantage/disadvantage record both attempts and tie-break to the first
nodes.rationale: Both attempts stay visible for the dice UI; a tie deterministically keeps attempt 0 in both modes.

nodes.label: onMutation fires exactly once per successful mutation, never for rollDice
nodes.rationale: Autosave and UI refresh hang off this hook, so a double fire double-saves and a missed fire loses state. rollDice is pure and must not trigger it; rerollWithLuck does, because it spends luck.

nodes.label: Damage floors hp at 0 with hp-zero; heal clamps at maxHp
nodes.rationale: hp-zero is emitted only when hp actually reaches 0; NaN, fractional, zero, negative and out-of-range amounts are all rejected as ok:false rather than clamped silently.

nodes.label: XP crosses multiple thresholds at once; luck +1 per level, capped at 3
nodes.rationale: A single large award must apply every hp increment it earns, grant a luck point per level gained, and still respect the cap of 3 -- and must not touch luck at all without a level-up.

nodes.label: Gold can never go negative and the error states the current balance
nodes.rationale: Zero deltas, fractional deltas and magnitudes over 100000 are rejected too.

nodes.label: A quest reward survives status updates that omit it
nodes.rationale: Set trimmed on creation, overwritten only by a non-empty value; an omitted or whitespace-only reward on update leaves the existing one alone.

nodes.label: Notes/facts collections cap and drop the oldest
nodes.rationale: Quest notes 20, NPC facts 20 (deduped), world facts 200 -- unbounded growth would blow the context brief. Quests and NPCs match case-insensitively by title/name so the DM's loose casing does not fork records.

nodes.label: Roll messages carry a documented shape and DC verdict suffix
nodes.rationale: The exact string is what the player and the model both read: no DC suffix when dc is absent, 'vs DC N -- checkmark success' when the total meets OR beats dc, failure otherwise. An invalid expression wraps into ok:false rather than throwing.

nodes.label: rerollWithLuck spends the luck even when the reroll is worse
nodes.rationale: The better of the two totals is kept and the message says so; luck at 0 rejects with an EngineResult error rather than throwing.

nodes.label: Race resolves from a preset ID as well as a display name
nodes.rationale: The web wizard renders race cards from /api/presets and posts back the preset ID, not the display name. Matching on name alone silently zeroed every web-created character's racial bonuses and stored race as 'elf', which rendered as 'elf Rogue' in the HUD and went to the DM that way. canonicalRaceName must also pass an unrecognized string through unchanged so old saves and custom races survive a round trip.

nodes.label: An explicit stats map is honored verbatim, not re-sorted by class priority
nodes.rationale: The web wizard's manual assignment must survive; racial bonuses land on top of it rather than replacing it.

nodes.label: maxHp floors at 1 and the AC dex bonus clamps to [0,+2]
nodes.rationale: Degenerate stat pools must not produce a 0-HP or AC-penalized character.

nodes.label: Campaign slugs collide into -2/-3 and creation writes nothing to disk
nodes.rationale: Creation is pure: it also copies starter items rather than sharing preset array/object references, so mutating a new character cannot poison the presets for the next one.

nodes.label: createNewHero keeps campaign/world/chronicle and rebuilds only the character
nodes.rationale: Identity-equal references to the three preserved sections, a character computed exactly as createNewCampaign would for the same class/race/stats, and no mutation of the existing state.

nodes.label: Only the access-code hash is stored, never the code
nodes.rationale: The registry file is asserted not to contain the normalized code. Codes are 96 bits in six hex groups and distinct across 200 draws; the registry is written owner-only (no group/other bits).

nodes.label: Dashes, spaces and case are insignificant in an access code
nodes.rationale: Players retype these by hand, so the hash must be computed over the canonical form. Empty, undefined and punctuation-only inputs still authenticate to nobody.

nodes.label: A player id can never escape the players directory
nodes.rationale: 'a/../../etc/passwd' slugifies to 'a-etc-passwd' and '../../escape' still resolves inside baseDir. Two names that collide into one id are refused outright -- they would share a save directory.

nodes.label: A corrupt registry degrades to 'no players' rather than throwing
nodes.rationale: A throw here would take the whole server down on boot; single-player PIN mode is the safe fallback. Malformed rows are dropped instead of trusted.

nodes.label: touchLastSeen throttles instead of rewriting the registry per request
nodes.rationale: This runs on every authenticated request -- actions, rolls, SSE connects. Unthrottled it was a synchronous read-modify-write on the hot path, and with two players active the pairs could interleave and drop a timestamp. A genuinely stale timestamp still triggers a write; the file mtime is asserted unchanged across a 25-call burst.

nodes.label: Registry cache invalidates on mtime and hands out copies
nodes.rationale: The no-restart switch from PIN mode to code mode depends on the mtime invalidation, so it is load-bearing rather than an optimisation. A caller mutating the returned registry must not poison the cache.

nodes.label: Revoking access never deletes the player's campaigns
nodes.rationale: Rotating invalidates the previous code; revoking stops the code working but leaves save files on disk, and neither operation affects other players.

nodes.label: Saves are {schemaVersion,data} envelopes with an atomic write
nodes.rationale: No .tmp files survive a save, exactly four files are written, updatedAt is refreshed, and a tampered schemaVersion throws an error naming the file and both versions.

nodes.label: v1 saves gain luck:1 and empty background fields without clobbering
nodes.rationale: A pre-luck save must load and keep everything else untouched; if the fields somehow already exist they are preserved; a genuinely newer-than-supported version still throws rather than being silently migrated. Re-saving persists the current SCHEMA_VERSION.

nodes.label: v2 worlds gain Quest.reward defaulted to empty string
nodes.rationale: Same shape as the v1->v2 migration: default the new field, never clobber an existing one, tolerate an empty quests array, and persist v3 on re-save.

nodes.label: A campaign slug that resolves outside its save dir is refused
nodes.rationale: Per-player isolation works by scoping baseDir to the player's own folder, so an escaping slug escapes the isolation. path.join normalises '../alice/secret' straight into a sibling player's campaign; this was verified exploitable before the guard existed. deleteCampaign is protected by the same check.

nodes.label: A corrupt or missing hero file degrades the card, not the listing
nodes.rationale: The campaign must stay in the picker and stay resumable; listings sort newest-updated first and tolerate stray files and empty directories.

nodes.label: Transcript reading skips corrupt JSONL lines and keeps valid ones
nodes.rationale: A half-written line from a crash must not make the whole campaign history unreadable; a missing file reads as an empty array.

nodes.label: deleteCampaign retires into .deleted rather than destroying
Missing settings.json is created with haiku/claude defaults, no warning
nodes.rationale: A second call must not rewrite the file, and a pre-P1 file that omits dmBackend/openai defaults them silently rather than warning.

nodes.label: A malformed settings.json warns but is never overwritten on disk
nodes.rationale: loadSettings never throws and never destroys a player's file mid-edit. Invalid fields are replaced individually (a bad dmModel does not discard a valid summarizerModel) and each fallback carries a warning.

nodes.label: 'dual' and narratorModel validate as first-class settings
nodes.rationale: A non-string narratorModel or a model-less openai block falls back to the default openai config with a warning while still honoring a valid dmBackend; an unknown dmBackend falls back to 'claude'.

nodes.label: env > file > built-in default, per field, with blanks treated as unset
nodes.rationale: Each DND_OPENAI_* var overrides independently and leaves the others (and dmBackend) alone; a whitespace-only value is unset rather than an override to ''; an invalid DND_DM_BACKEND is ignored without throwing. The OPENROUTER_API_KEY convenience default only fills an apiKeyEnv nobody configured.

nodes.label: Referee resolves mechanics, narrator writes prose from ground truth
nodes.rationale: The architectural bet of the dual backend: a reliable tool-caller owns state, a permissive prose model owns voice, and everything the narrator is allowed to say is derived from what the referee actually did. Every dualDm invariant is a consequence of enforcing that split against weak free-tier models.

hyperedges.label: Keeping a weak referee/narrator pair mechanically honest
SUGGEST trailer: asked for, parsed, then stripped from every durable surface
dmBackend fans out to three independent routing decisions
